峡.meaning: On a ledge between steep <part>mountain</part> walls, three hikers meet a goat coming the other way. The only way past is a tight <part>group hug</part>, goat included, shuffling sideways over the drop. Far below, a river roars through the <kanji>gorge</kanji>.
峡.on: A hiker reads the goat's collar tag aloud, stretching the start so it echoes off the walls: '<sound>Kyo</sound>to!'
峡.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' bleats the goat, and trots off to the ba<sound>za</sound>ar on the far side to find its <sound>ma</sound>ma.

秩.meaning: A farmer plants her <part>grain</part> in perfect rows, one stalk per step. When a single stalk goes missing, she'd rather <part>lose</part> the whole field than leave a gap, so she replants it at midnight with a ruler. Her farm runs on strict <kanji>regularity</kanji>.
秩.on: Each row is guarded by a <sound>chee</sound>tah that sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' at every crow.

羅.meaning: A beekeeper makes her own veil. She unpicks an old fishing <part>net</part> and reweaves each <part>fiber</part> finer and finer, until bees can't get through but sunlight can. It floats over her hat like a cloud of <kanji>gauze</kanji>.
羅.on: Her bees buzz around her like cheerleaders: '<sound>Rah</sound>!'
羅.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>ps,' she says, as a bee lands on her <sound>su</sound>shi; a <sound>mo</sound>th taps the veil, and she whispers, '<sound>No</sound>t you either.'

賄.meaning: In a beach court, a crab on trial slides a pearl-filled <part>shellfish</part> under the seagull judge's wing. Eager to <part>possess</part> that pearl, the gull bangs his gavel: not guilty! Every crab on the sand saw the <kanji>bribe</kanji>.
賄.on: '<sound>Why</sound>?' squawks a second gull, who wanted a pearl too.
賄.kun: The crab's <sound>ma</sound>ma pays the court fees, <sound>ca</sound>lmly counting out <sound>na</sound>chos, then drops one: '<sound>Oo</sound>ps.' She provides for everything.

塾.meaning: After school the kids want a <part>ball game</part>, but their parents send them down to a classroom dug into the <part>soil</part> under the playground, doing sums till nine. Above them, the ball bounces alone. That basement is the <kanji>cram school</kanji>.
塾.on: A <sound>ju</sound>ry of moles marks their tests and hands out one <sound>coo</sound>kie each.

懲.meaning: In the cat court, the goldfish thief must sit in the window wearing a <part>sign</part> that says 'I ate the goldfish', his little <part>heart</part> sinking every time a bird laughs. Cat law is strict, and its <kanji>penal</kanji> code is very public.
懲.on: The sign hangs from a tight <sound>cho</sound>ker of jingling bells.
懲.kun: Next day he walks past the <sound>ko</sound>i pond and its <sound>ree</sound>ds without one glance: lesson learned.

掌.meaning: At the bakery awards, the judge holds the winning bun up high on one flat <part>hand</part>, like a waiter with a tray: the cake held in the greatest <part>esteem</part>. Warm crumbs gather in the hollow of her <kanji>palm</kanji>.
掌.on: Then she bows to the crowd: the bun is the star of the <sound>show</sound>.
掌.kun: A <sound>te</sound>nnis fan bumps her ('Oh, <sound>no</sound>t again!'), and the bun bounces off a <sound>hee</sound>l into a bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men.
